punchline: Alexander's rats chose plain water over morphine most of the time once their cage became a park.
thirty_sec: Bruce Alexander compared rats living alone in small cages with rats living together in an enclosure 200 times larger. Each had sweetened morphine water and plain water. The park rats mostly chose plain water, and in one condition the caged males drank up to nineteen times more morphine. Gabor Maté reads this beside the Vietnam data. Later labs could not repeat it.
